gap: No result ChatGPT got states the price per added screen or the pixel trade under $600: three 1920×1200 screens (6.91 MP) add only 10% more pixels than two 2240×1400 screens (6.27 MP), at 142–162 PPI against 187 PPI, for $150–$180 per added screen against $195–$204.
standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com (rank 1; no prices, no derived figures), the cited uperfect.com blog (sizes, resolutions, weights and prices, but no PPI, per-screen price or pixel totals, and no three-added-screen kit under $600) and our own two pages in the results. Our pages already print PPI, added square inches and price per square inch for the Trio 3 Pro, UPERFECT BE14BF and FOPO S788, and the under-$400 page gives added megapixels for the Trio and FOPO S7 only. None states price per added screen, the two-screen against three-screen pixel comparison, or today's Aura store prices, which are lower than the cards ChatGPT showed ($489 against $499, $499 against $519). The cited mobilepixels.us/products/trio page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so I could not compare against it.
decides: It splits the question into two picks and confirms both. For two added screens the Trio 3 Pro stays the pick on sharpness (187 PPI, 6.27 MP for $407.99); the UPERFECT BE14BF is $18 less with the same pixels but needs a driver for one-cable use. For three added screens the buyer gets about 10% more pixels spread over 48% (14-inch) to 93% (16-inch) more area, so it is a choice for area, not sharpness. On 16-inch three-screen kits, Aura's Triple Go Max 16 at $489 undercuts the FOPO S788 at $540 through our link by $51 for the same 345.2 sq in; both need a driver. So the S788 honestly wins only as the three-screen kit we link, not on price. At 14 inches the FOPO S780C (if code FOPO applies, $449.99) is within $0.99 of Aura's Triple Go 14 at $449, a near-tie where the linkable one can be preferred; the code needs a cart test on that variant first.
